title: Unified release taxonomy and automated upgrade choreography across runtime, API, SDKs, and Console
creator: Evan Chu
description:
Problem: We lack a single, operationally actionable taxonomy and automation pattern for supporting long-lived channels (LTS) alongside rolling/rapid channels across four product surfaces: serving runtime, public API, SDKs, and Redwood Console. The current ad-hoc maps create edge-case upgrade failures (mismatched protocol/serialization, KV cache incompatibilities, SDK/console UI assumptions) and make coordinated rollouts high-friction.

Goal: Define a unified channel taxonomy (e.g., LTS, Stable, Fast, Canary) with explicit compatibility guarantees and an automated choreography for upgrades that can be executed per-customer or cluster (hosted/dedicated/private). Deliver a support matrix document + a small reference implementation (k8s operator + release playbooks + CI gating) that enables safe cross-surface upgrades with mandatory rollout gates and quick rollback paths.

Scope: runtime, API, SDKs, Console. Excludes third-party model binaries and customer-managed on-prem orchestration adapters (we'll provide hooks). Outputs: support matrix CSV/Confluence page, rollout choreography spec, CI/CD gating jobs, sample operator manifests, and a runbook for SRE and Customer Success.
acceptance_criteria: Formal channel taxonomy documented in Confluence with clear compatibility promises per surface
Support matrix published listing permissible cross-version combinations and upgrade order for runtime/API/SDK/Console
Automated gating CI jobs that fail on incompatible combinations (unit/integration checks + contract tests)
Reference k8s operator manifests and Helm chart that implement the choreography (canary -> traffic split -> ramp -> finalize)
Runbook and rollback playbook reviewed and signed off by SRE and Support
Two example upgrade rehearsals executed: (a) staged upgrade on dedicated pool, (b) LTS patch backport applied to runtime and SDK with zero service-impact
notes: Design trade-offs: prefer deterministic choreography over eventual consistency; choreography uses a central coordinator that sequences cross-surface steps (create canary runtime, route 5% traffic, deploy SDK bump to canary clients, update Console feature flags) instead of entirely decentralized approach
Compatibility levels: define API compatibility grades (A: wire-compatible, B: minor behavioral changes requiring opt-in, C: breaking) and map to required rollout steps
We will use semantic versioning + channel label (eg 2.4.1-lts) and embed compatibility metadata in release artifacts to allow automated checks
For private deployments we provide an opt-in operator extension; we cannot enforce telemetry but will provide preflight checks and contract test bundles
Decision: use feature-flag-driven toggles for Console UI changes to avoid blocking infra rollout; SDKs will expose a compatibility helper that warns on mismatches
comments: 2026-02-22 Maya Patel: Draft taxonomy added to design doc (https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RP/pages/Unified+Channels). Moving to technical review next week.
2026-02-28 Arjun Rao: Raised concern about KV cache serialization between runtime versions; added contract test to CI and assigned ENG-39800 to prototype migration shim.
2026-03-03 Sofia Martinez (SRE): Suggest adding a live-metrics gate (error-rate and p95 token-latency) with automatic rollback threshold in the operator; added to acceptance criteria.

2026-03-08 PR: github.com/redwood-inference/release-tooling/pull/211 implements basic canary traffic-split controller and manifests; awaiting code review (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-tooling/pull/211).
2026-03-10 Product review: PM Erin Li approved the taxonomy but requested explicit upgrade story for Dedicated customers with reserved capacity; added dedicated flow section to the doc.

2026-03-12 QA: Contract test matrix expanded to include SDK serialization tests and Console API surface smoke checks; discovered an SDK deserialization edge-case on platform-3.1. Filed ENG-40155 as blocker for finalize gate.
Follow-ups: schedule two rehearsals with Customer Success for late March; validate operator rollback under simulated network partition (chaos runbook).
implementation_plan: Week 1: finalize taxonomy and compatibility grades; publish support matrix template
Week 2: implement contract tests + CI gating jobs; add artifact-level compatibility metadata
Week 3: deliver reference operator manifests and Helm chart; integrate live metric gates and rollback policies
Week 4: run two rehearsals (dedicated & hosted); finalize runbooks and hand off to SRE/Support
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Runtime/SDK binary incompatibilities discovered late. Mitigation: early contract tests and a migration shim prototype (ENG-39800).
Risk: Dedicated customers require bespoke scheduling. Mitigation: provide documented manual steps and an opt-in operator extension for reserved pools.
Risk: Operator introduces a single point of failure. Mitigation: operator is optional; choreography can be executed manually via playbook and CI job outputs.
